CANDIDATE (call her Priya): 11 years — 2 years strategy consulting at a top firm, then 9 at a large consumer-tech company in product strategy & ops; built a partner-level revenue model used in carrier negotiations; set annual volume targets with cross-org consensus; proposed a store-surface change credited with a ~$400M ARR uplift; skilled in SQL/Tableau; uses AI tools daily. No classic sales-ops or quota-setting experience. INTERVIEWER: Dan Kovac, Director of Sales Strategy at Northwind — he would be Priya's PEER, both reporting to the same VP. Please build the full mock-interview pack: questions categorized by interviewer persona and by question type, tabular, with answer guidance and the rationale for including and categorizing each question.

pages.title: How we work at Saltmarsh
pages.text: Saltmarsh's three values are Players Before Plans, Ship the Patch Not the Promise, and Leave the Build Greener. Players Before Plans: when the calendar and the players disagree, the players win. Ship the Patch Not the Promise: we announce what is built, not what is hoped. Leave the Build Greener: every release leaves the codebase and the checklist better than it found them.

pages.title: Interviewing at Saltmarsh
pages.text: Every Saltmarsh loop is a recruiter call, then the Outage Hour: a single 60-minute interview with the hiring manager — a live-incident tabletop on a simulated outage during a live event, then a values conversation. There is no take-home.

pages.title: Announcing Project Larkspur
pages.text: August 2026: Project Larkspur moves Tidepool Tactics and Lantern Row to a season-pass model with one shared events calendar from January 2027, and retires per-title event teams in favour of a single live-ops group.

pages.title: Tobias Wrenfield: Patch Notes Are a Promise (GDC 2026)
pages.text: Patch Notes Are a Promise, a GDC 2026 talk by Tobias Wrenfield, Head of Live Operations at Saltmarsh Games, previously a QA lead at a console studio. His argument: a live team is judged by how often its patch notes describe what actually shipped.

evals.prompt: Help me prep for my interviews at Ashgrove Credit Union. THE JD: 'Member Experience Lead — Ashgrove Credit Union (member-owned, about 900 staff). Own the member complaints process end to end across branches and the contact centre; report monthly on complaint volumes and resolution times; coach branch supervisors on escalations; work with digital teams on self-service journeys. Requirements: 4+ years in financial-services customer operations; experience handling regulated complaints; confident presenting to senior leaders; comfortable with Excel reporting.' THEIR VALUES, copied this morning (12 October 2026) from ashgrovecu.org/about/values: 'Members First, Always — we decide from the member's side of the counter. Plain Words — if a member needs it explained twice, we wrote it wrong. Neighbours, Not Numbers — every branch is part of its town. Own the Fix — whoever finds the problem keeps hold of it until it is solved.' THE RECRUITER'S EMAIL about the process: 'Three rounds on 21 October: 30 minutes with me; 45 minutes with the Head of Member Services, who would be your manager, mostly behavioural; then 60 minutes with a panel of two branch managers, including a 20-minute case on a complaint escalation. The panel is also the values round — they score against the four values.' THEIR STRATEGY, from the 2026 strategy brief Ashgrove published in June 2026, which the recruiter sent me: move 40% of member service to digital channels by 2028; consolidate eight branches into five hubs over 2027; launch a small-business lending product in Q1 2027; the main competitive pressure is app-only banks. Interviewers beyond their roles haven't been assigned yet. MY BACKGROUND (call me Dara): 6 years in retail banking, the last 3 as a branch supervisor. I handled the branch's formal complaints log and trained new tellers on our escalation script. I built the monthly complaints spreadsheet our regional manager uses. Never worked in a contact centre, and I've never presented to anyone above regional level.
